clause_correction: The Stage R rejection clause was mis-stated: a high axial fraction means the soma segment's rise is set by how fast its neighbours can be charged, which makes the load more able to be the lever, not less. mechanism_reading: At the fastest rise the soma segment receives 2.5 to 3.1 nA of sodium current, passes 2.2 to 2.6 nA on to its neighbours, and keeps 0.4 to 0.7 nA to charge its own capacitance. dV/dt = (I_Na - I_axial - I_K - I_leak + I_applied) / C_segment. The candidate's slower sodium opening (factor 2) cuts the sodium current by 20 percent and the retained capacitive current by 37 percent; the human's 351 V/s needs the retained current cut by another 45 percent, by less sodium, more load, or slower opening still.
